title: Sessions opens hearing on identity verification to address evolving fraud threats
text:
Sessions opens hearing on identity verification to address evolving fraud threats
Subcommittee on Government Operations Chairman Pete Sessions delivered opening remarks at a hearing titled “Emerging Fraud Threats and the Evolving Fraud Landscape” in Washington on July 15. Sessions said that changes made to Login.gov over the years have left vulnerabilities, allowing fraudsters to create thousands of synthetic identities and apply for various government programs simultaneously. He said federal agencies need to be proactive in preventing fraud by identifying new methods used by scammers.
Sessions welcomed attendees, saying, “Welcome to today’s hearing on emerging threats and the evolving fraud landscape.” He emphasized the importance of focusing on prevention before fraud occurs, stating, “As we’ve heard countless times before, once money has gone out the door, it’s hard to get that money back.”
He outlined several types of fraud previously discussed by the subcommittee, including foreign actors applying for disaster relief programs and elaborate rings exploiting benefits program loopholes. Sessions noted that identity fraud is increasing as fraudulent actors use advanced tools such as artificial intelligence: “Identity fraud threats, specifically, are booming as fraudulent actors become smarter and gain access to tools intended to make our lives easier—namely, AI.”
Sessions referenced a March 2023 subcommittee hearing about Login.gov following findings from the General Services Administration Inspector General report. He said GSA misled clients regarding whether Login.gov met technical standards needed for secure identity verification. According to Sessions, ongoing changes have prompted federal agencies to explore other digital identity solutions.
“Fraudsters...can now create hundreds or thousands of synthetic identities and apply for many different government benefits programs simultaneously,” he said. He also warned about deep fakes being used to bypass safeguards.
Sessions concluded by highlighting bipartisan legislation he introduced in January—the Stop Identity Fraud and Identity Theft Act—which aims “to strengthen the nation’s digital identity verification infrastructure and protect individuals, businesses and government programs from rapidly rising identity fraud and theft.” He expressed hope that discussions at the hearing would help improve this legislation.
summary: Sessions said that changes made to Login.gov over the years have left vulnerabilities, allowing fraudsters to create thousands of synthetic identities and apply for various government programs simultaneously.
